messages:
sara_sales: Quick question from the customer POC — they want PrivateLink to our Private deployment but also need SFTP traffic routed to their on-prem via their TGW. Asking about split-horizon DNS + egress NAT. Any immediate blockers?

alex_g: We can support that topology but need to clarify who initiates connections to on-prem. PrivateLink (interface endpoints) is inbound into our service from their VPC. If their TGW must carry egress to 192.168.50.0/24, the routing must be on their side. Do we need our runtime to reach into their onprem, or just respond to callbacks?

net_eng_tom: A few quick notes: PrivateLink creates ENIs in the customer VPC. It does not automatically create routes from our VPC to their TGW. For split-horizon DNS they should use Route53 Resolver inbound/outbound endpoints or conditional forwarders (or a delegated private hosted zone) — otherwise the interface endpoint will resolve to our IPs and not the onprem names.

sara_sales: They gave CIDRs: onprem 192.168.50.0/24, corp VPC 10.10.0.0/16. Requirements: model traffic over PrivateLink, SFTP out to 192.168.50.0/24 via their TGW, and strict egress allowlist on our side.

security_bob: From security questionnaire perspective — acceptable. We'll require explicit firewall rules and egress SNAT control. Example minimal rules they can expect from our Dedicated/Private runtime:

```
# Redwood-managed outbound ACL (example)
ALLOW tcp 443 -> <customer-privatelink-enis> (our service control plane & runtime)
ALLOW tcp 22  -> 192.168.50.0/24   # SFTP to on-prem
ALLOW udp 53  -> 10.10.0.2         # DNS resolver (if using customer resolver)
DENY  all other outbound
```

We also need logging to S3 or their syslog for compliance.

net_eng_tom: If their TGW expects traffic with source from our IP ranges, they may want SNAT to a predictable public/private pool. We can front egress through an egress-proxy that does SNAT from a dedicated SNAT pool. Alternative (often simpler): they host a small proxy in their VPC and we call it via PrivateLink back to them — then they handle TGW->onprem routing.

alex_g: Pricing question they asked: does PrivateLink add a per-GB or endpoint-hour cost? Short answer: yes — AWS charges their side for interface endpoint hours and data processing. On Redwood side we invoice data transfer + reserved capacity per contract. I'll draft an estimate (small infra setup + per-GB transfer).

sara_sales: Can we put together a runbook / checklist to send them? They want to move fast and validate during the POC this week. Also need the minimal firewall matrix for their security review.

net_eng_tom: I'll draft a network runbook. Items to include:
- Customer: create interface endpoint(s) for our service in their VPC/subnets (AZ-redundant).
- Customer: route table entries for subnets that should reach PrivateLink (no special routes needed for interface endpoints unless egress to TGW is required).
- Customer: Route53 resolver inbound/outbound or conditional forwarder for split-horizon DNS (share zone names).
- Customer: TGW route for 192.168.50.0/24 -> onprem. Ensure not to override interface endpoint routes.
- Redwood: Provide SNAT pool if runtime must initiate egress to onprem; otherwise we prefer they host an egress proxy.
- Security: firewall ACL sample (see above) + log delivery and approvals.

security_bob: I'll produce the firewall matrix and a short justification for each rule for the security questionnaire. Also note: MFA + cert pinning requirements for SFTP endpoints, and we should document retention for SFTP logs.

alex_g: Action items: sara_sales -> confirm whether our runtime needs to initiate connections to 192.168.50.0/24 or if customer will proxy inbound; net_eng_tom -> runbook + SNAT options; security_bob -> firewall matrix; alex_g -> pricing estimate.

sara_sales: On it — pinging customer now. ETA: will push CIDR confirmation and expected egress throughput (they said ~1 TB/day) by EOD. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Reminder: created internal ticket INF-8492 for POC connectivity work (assignee: net_eng_tom).
